in_latin.name: Adeodatus
in_latin.meaning: Name meaning God-given, gift of God, or God is a gift
in_latin.long_meaning: Adeodatus est nomen quod significat donum Dei, datum a Deo aut Deus est donum. Nomina similis, ut Deus, sunt communia in multarum linguarum culturis et religiosis traditionibus. Adeodatus est Latinum nomen, ab a- (nihil) et deus (Deus), signum quod Deus non dedit, donum a Deo datum. In Christiana traditione, nomen Adeodatus designat donum a Deo, gratiam a Deo datam. Nomen est usitatum in Ecclesia Catholica et in cultura Christiana. In contextu scripturali, nomen Adeodatus non est expressum, sed significatio eius est manifesta in scripturis sacris, ubi Deus est donum a Deo datum hominibus.

in_english.long_meaning: Adeodatus is a name that means gift of God, given by God, or God is a gift. Names similar to God are common in many languages and religious traditions. Adeodatus is a Latin name, from a- (nothing) and deus (God), signifying that God did not give, but a gift given by God. In Christian tradition, the name Adeodatus signifies a gift from God, grace given by God. The name is used in the Catholic Church and in Christian culture. In scriptural context, the name Adeodatus is not explicitly stated, but its meaning is evident in sacred scriptures, where God is a gift given by God to humans.

historical_references.reference: Adeodatus of Vienne was a bishop in the late 4th century. He was a disciple of Saint Germanus of Auxerre and played an important role in the spread of Christianity in Gaul. He is venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic Church.
Saint Adeodatus of Toulouse was a bishop in the 6th century. He is traditionally considered the first bishop of Toulouse and was martyred during the early Muslim invasions of the Iberian Peninsula.
